title: Affine formal modules: Limit
statement: Let A be a Noetherian commutative ring, I an ideal, B its I-adic completion, X=Spec A, and J the quasi-coherent ideal sheaf associated to I (the notions in the statement dependencies). There exists a functor L from coherent formal J-modules on X to finite B-modules and, for every formal system F, a cone p(F) from restricted L(F) to the A-module tower Gamma(F_n). Here index n denotes positive level n+1. Every cone is limiting. The projections commute with L(f) for every morphism of formal systems f. Each nth projection is surjective with kernel I^(n+1)L(F) as an A-submodule. For r in B with residue represented by a in A at level n+1, p(F)_n(r x)=a p(F)_n(x). No equivalence, inverse functor, unit or counit is asserted.

proof.text: Apply the affine-sections bridge to every coherent formal system. It gives the finite-level annihilation, finiteness and successor-kernel hypotheses.

Construct each completed module and its A-linear comparison with the ordinary limit using the completed scalar theorem. Apply the algebraic finite-limit theorem to obtain finiteness and the projection kernel formula.

For a morphism f transport lim(Gamma(f)) along the two limit comparisons. The limit-map projection equation gives naturality. To prove completion-linearity, choose an A-representative of the completed scalar at each coordinate; apply the residue equation in source and target and A-linearity of the coordinate map. Joint injectivity of projections proves equality.

Identity and composition follow by conjugating the ordinary limit functor maps and cancelling inverse comparisons. Lift the resulting functor to the full finite-module subcategory. Extend the ordinary limit cone along its comparison isomorphism; this cone is limiting. The finite-limit theorem supplies surjectivity and kernels, and the completed scalar theorem supplies the final equation.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentFormalModules_affine_limit (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (J : (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)).IdealSheafData)
    (hJ : J = Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
      (I.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv.hom)) :
    ∃ L : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J ⥤
      ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
      (fun N : ModuleCat.{u} (AdicCompletion I A) ↦ Module.Finite (AdicCompletion I A) N),
    ∃ p : ∀ F : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J,
      (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ).obj
        ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).obj
          (L.obj F).obj) ⟶ F.obj ⋙ moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of A),
    (∀ F, Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk _ (p F)))) ∧
    (∀ (F G : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J) (f : F ⟶ G)
      (n : ℕ),
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).map
        (L.map f).hom ≫ (p G).app (op n) =
      (p F).app (op n) ≫ (moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of A)).map (f.hom.app (op n))) ∧
    (∀ (F : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J) (n : ℕ),
      Function.Surjective ((p F).app (op n)) ∧
      LinearMap.ker ((p F).app (op n)).hom =
        I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A
          ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).obj
            (L.obj F).obj))) ∧
    (∀ (F : CoherentFormalModule (Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) J) (n : ℕ)
      (r : AdicCompletion I A) (a : A) (x : (L.obj F).obj),
      AdicCompletion.evalₐ I (n + 1) r = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1)) a →
      (p F).app (op n) (r • x) = a • (p F).app (op n) x)
